title: RMP vs TSG
summary: Sub Rogue / Frost Mage / Disc into Arms, Unholy and Resto Druid. Kill the Warrior through a Sap opener, and treat the Druid's Cyclone as the thing that actually beats you.

sections.title: Kill the Warrior, and expect to need two goes
sections.body:
Answer counts: the Warrior holds five (Die by the Sword, Rallying Cry, Berserker Shout, Spell Reflection, trinket). Rallying Cry is the one these guides keep leaving out, and it is the one that most changes what a failed go costs you — it is party-wide, so it does not save the Warrior, it blunts the entire attempt. The Death Knight holds six, two of them school-specific against exactly the damage this comp does — Anti-Magic Shell and Anti-Magic Zone are both answers to a Mage and a Priest, and Lichborne makes him immune to the fear.

So the Warrior is the target on count, and by a wider margin than usual against a caster comp: half the DK's kit is built to ignore you.

The argument against, and it is real: the Warrior has a charge, a leap and a knockback, so he is the harder of the two to hold still. If your Rogue cannot stay on him you are choosing a target you cannot actually pin, which is the trade-off this plan does not resolve.

sections.title: Opener — Sap, then set up on the Warrior

steps.note: On the Druid. It is free, so the opener costs nothing before it starts.
Also free. Same category as the Sap, so it lands halved — but it buys the Rogue the reposition, and nothing else is spent.
On the Warrior. Twelve seconds, the cheapest real stun in the game and the reason this opener repeats.
Same category as Cheap Shot, so it is halved. Worth it here only because the go is already committed — otherwise hold it.

sections.title: Keep the healer out — the real chain

steps.note: Fresh category after the Sap and Polymorph, so this is the first control on the Druid at full duration.
Incapacitate again and therefore diminished — the argument for it is that it needs no target and covers the reposition.
GUESS: this is a two-minute cooldown and it is the last thing in the chain, so it lands diminished. Holding it as a peel on the Warrior may be worth more than three seconds here.

sections.title: Shut the Death Knight off the go

steps.note: Cheap, and it costs him the global he would spend on Anti-Magic Zone.
Root rather than a stun — he still acts, but he is not on your Mage, and it shares no category with anything above.
On the Mage. Two minutes, so it is only in every second attempt.
Channelled, so it needs the Warrior actually held rather than merely slowed.
On the Mage, before the damage rather than during it.
Short enough to be back every go, and it eats a Polymorph or a Blast. Do not open into it.
The one that actually costs him something.
Answers the Scream for free, which is why the Scream goes to the Druid.
Party-wide, so it blunts the whole go rather than saving one player.

sections.title: What the Death Knight brings to the fight

steps.note: Back inside one cadence, and it answers most of what a Mage and a Priest do.
Party-wide magic mitigation — the reason a caster go into a stacked TSG can achieve nothing.
Fear immunity. Your Scream and your Blind both stop working on him while it is up.
Not a defensive: it is a silence, and it is what stops the Priest saving the kill target.

sections.title: Cadence: everything lands on thirty, except what matters most
sections.body:
Cheap Shot at twelve seconds is out on its own and effectively always available. Then the thirty-second tier: Kidney Shot, Psychic Scream, Gouge, Tricks of the Trade, Flurry, Ice Barrier, Crimson Vial.

The real goes are gated much higher — Shadow Blades and Power Infusion sit far above that tier, so the comp gets many small attempts and few genuine ones. That is the shape of the matchup: repeated cheap pressure to strip their answers, with the committed attempt saved for when the Warrior has nothing.

Blind and Ice Block are both two-minute answers, and the side that spends theirs first usually loses the round.

sections.title: Where this is guessing
sections.body:
1. The Blind. This plan spends it in the healer chain where it lands diminished, which is probably wrong — as a peel on the Warrior at full duration it may force the trinket without a stun. I could not settle it.

2. Cyclone is not in any section above, and it is the ability most likely to beat this comp. Nothing here says what to do about a Resto Druid cycloning your Mage mid-go, because I do not know whether the answer is to pre-empt it with a silence or to eat it and go again.

3. Anti-Magic Zone against a two-caster comp may make the whole plan wrong rather than merely slower — perhaps the Warrior is not the target at all when it is up.

4. Whether the opener should Sap the Druid or the Death Knight. This plan assumes the healer, and against a DK who can Lichborne out of everything else, that assumption is not obvious.
